messages:
sasha: Heads-up — noticed a flurry of dedicated-slice evictions in eu-west-2 between 00:12-00:15. lots of small tenants spiking and our soft-evict window is tripping fast.

kai: Can you paste the eviction histogram? is it CPU, memory, or egress that triggered it?

sasha: egress spike + KV cache churn. eviction events look like this in the logs:
```
[2026-06-12T00:13:21Z] evicting slice tenant=acme-ml reason=egress_surge score=87 cache_miss=0.73
[2026-06-12T00:13:22Z] preempting slice tenant=acme-ml fallback=quantized-2bit
```

marta: ugh. acme-ml is on fractional dedicated. they lease 0.5 slice but burst to 2x for inference spikes. our routing sent their tail to the warm pool which then starved their prefix cache.

lee: Could we add a short "safety net" holdback that keeps KV cache pinned for N seconds after preempt to avoid immediate quality regressions? cost impact might be minimal if N small (5-30s).

kai: There's an interplay with routing: if we delay eviction, we hold capacity and block bursty tenants behind the lane. Need a SLA-aware decision: high-tier tenants get cache hold, others get immediate preempt.

sasha: Agreed. Proposal: when preempting fractional dedicated slices, set cache_retention=15s for customers with tier >= standard and request_rate_last_min > 10 rps. Also set a cap on total retained memory per host.

marta: Implementation note — retention should be a soft flag in the allocator so fallback routing doesn't assume cache cold. Otherwise callers will immediately re-request big prefixes.

kai: Also tie into routing policy: if held slice still hot, prefer funneling their requests through a proxy path with reduced parallelism rather than get full warm-pool capacity. That reduces inter-tenant egress.

lee: Quick cost calc: if average cached memory held per slice = 2GB, retention window 15s, global concurrent holds peak=200 -> 400GB-s = 0.11 GB-hours per event. negligible at scale, but need per-host guardrails.

sasha: Ops question — how do we surface this to SRE/CS when it triggers? right now only logs. we should emit a signal with tag `eviction_safety_net` so CS can message customers when quality might dip briefly.

marta: +1. Let's also add a metric `allocator.eviction_hold_count` and per-tenant label. keep retention on by default for "standard+" and opt-out via tenant policy.

kai: Sounds workable. I'll draft a minimal allocator change: add retention TTL and per-host mem_budget check. can we ship as a feature flag in eu-west-2 only for 48h?

lee: roll it canary -> 10% hosts -> monitor p99 latency, miss-rate, and evictions. If p99 increases or evictions drop by >30% with cost within X, expand.

infra-bot: deploy-plan created by kai: canary: eu-west-2 10% -> 25% -> 100% over 72h. monitors: allocator.eviction_hold_count, p99-gen-latency, egress-saturation.

sasha: Perfect. tagging @oncall to watch 00:00-04:00 window tomorrow. thanks team. :thumbsup:
